what_happened: The operator thought PR #180 landed slowly because the early pull request opened after Athena's checks. On that guess they queued job 20261025-110525-8hzb without reading run.rs. The code already opens the early pull request before the checks (run.rs:1645), so the critic stopped the job as a misread of the code. The real cause is a race. The early CI run takes about 16 minutes. Athena's checks and verifier take about 14. The landing run therefore starts before the early run's pass is cached. This also corrects the earlier record 20261025-110528-10mv.
cause: A request about pipeline speed is written from an assumed stage order and assumed causes. Athena has no current record of the stage order and measured durations, including CI duration against the checks-plus-verifier time. Neither request intake nor the reading checks a diagnosis of a timing problem against the code or against measured timings. The error is found only after a job has been paid for, and each wrong diagnosis then needs a further correction record.
prevention: Keep a generated, current stage timeline: the order of stages in run.rs and the measured duration of each, including how long CI takes. Before any request that claims a cause for a timing problem, check the claim against this timeline. The reading must cite the stage order and durations it relies on, and the critic must reject a speed request whose premise contradicts the timeline. This would have shown that the early PR already opens before the checks and that the 16-minute CI run is longer than the 14-minute checks and verifier.
proposed_request: Make the landing run reuse the early pull request's CI result even when that CI run is still in progress. Background: the early pull request already opens before Athena's checks (run.rs:1645). Its CI run takes about 16 minutes. Athena's checks and verifier take about 14 minutes. The landing run therefore starts before the early run's pass is cached, so it runs CI again and a landing takes about 18 minutes. Outcome: when a landing finds the early run for the same commit still in progress, it waits for that run, or reuses its result, instead of starting a full second CI run. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fake early run that is still pending at landing time shows the landing does not start a second CI run and uses the early run's result; (2) a failed early run still blocks the landing; (3) the stage order and durations measured for a real landing are recorded in the job summary, showing the landing time before and after. Before writing the plan, read run.rs and confirm the stage order and where the early pull request opens.
